# Wages and Enlistment at the Wall {#sec-did submitted="@tarly2025"}

This chapter shows how to write figures, tables, equations, theorems and citations.
Everything is numbered by chapter and appears in the lists at the front of the thesis.

## Figures

In the second year of the study, the Night's Watch raised the wage of new recruits at
Castle Black but not at Eastwatch-by-the-Sea. @fig-did shows monthly enlistment at both
castles.

![Enlistment at Castle Black and Eastwatch (simulated data). The dashed line is the
counterfactual for Castle Black under parallel trends.](../images/did.png){#fig-did
width=85%}

## Equations

The difference-in-differences estimator compares the change at the treated castle with
the change at the control castle:

$$
\hat\delta = \left(\bar y_{T,1} - \bar y_{T,0}\right) - \left(\bar y_{C,1} - \bar y_{C,0}\right).
$$ {#eq-did}

Equivalently, $\hat\delta$ is the interaction coefficient in the regression

$$
y_{it} = \alpha + \beta\,\text{Treat}_i + \gamma\,\text{Post}_t
  + \delta\,(\text{Treat}_i \times \text{Post}_t) + \varepsilon_{it}.
$$ {#eq-twfe}

Unnumbered display math has no label. The key assumption is parallel trends:

$$
E\left[y_{1}(0) - y_{0}(0) \mid T\right] = E\left[y_{1}(0) - y_{0}(0) \mid C\right].
$$

## Theorems and Proofs

::: {#prp-did}
## Identification

Under parallel trends, the difference-in-differences estimand equals the average
treatment effect on the treated.
:::

@prp-did is proved in @sec-app-proofs. Theorems (`#thm-`), lemmas (`#lem-`),
corollaries (`#cor-`), definitions (`#def-`), examples (`#exm-`) and remarks work the
same way.
